title: Underwriting
body: The process by which an insurance company evaluates an applicant's risk, determines whether to issue a policy, and sets the premium. Involves reviewing medical history, driving record, property details, and other risk factors.

title: Risk Assessment
body: The evaluation of potential losses an insurer might face from issuing a policy. Uses statistical models, historical data, and expert judgment to classify applicants into risk categories and determine appropriate pricing.

title: Actuarial Science
body: The mathematical discipline that uses statistics, financial mathematics, and probability theory to evaluate insurance risk and uncertainty. Actuaries design insurance products, set premiums, and ensure financial stability.

title: Claim
body: A formal request by an insured person to the insurance company for payment of benefits under the terms of the insurance policy for a covered loss or event.

title: Claims Lifecycle
body: The complete process from claim submission through settlement: reporting, investigation, validation, adjustment, and payment. Can span days to months depending on complexity and dispute.

title: Adjuster
body: A professional employed or authorized by an insurance company to investigate claims, verify policy coverage, determine liability, and estimate the cost of damages or losses.

title: Claim Investigation
body: The process of examining evidence, conducting interviews, reviewing documentation, and determining the validity and extent of a claim. Includes site inspections, medical review, and third-party verification.

title: Fraud Detection
body: The identification and prevention of fraudulent insurance claims through statistical analysis, pattern matching, network analysis, and investigative techniques. Protects insurers from intentional misrepresentation or false claims.

title: Claims Denials
body: When an insurance company refuses to pay a claim because it does not meet policy terms, is outside coverage, or is fraudulent. Must be documented with clear reasoning and policy references.

title: Reinsurance
body: Insurance purchased by insurance companies to protect themselves from catastrophic losses. A reinsurer assumes a portion of the original insurer's risk in exchange for a premium, enabling risk distribution.

title: Loss Ratio
body: A key metric calculated as claims paid divided by premiums collected. For example, a 0.75 loss ratio means the insurer pays $0.75 in claims for every $1.00 in premiums. Used to assess profitability and pricing adequacy.

title: Regulatory Compliance
body: Adherence to state and federal insurance laws, including rate approval, reserve requirements, solvency standards, and consumer protection regulations. Enforced by state insurance commissioners.

title: Reserve (Insurance Reserve)
body: Money set aside by an insurance company to pay future claims that have been incurred but not yet paid. Includes reserves for known claims (case reserves) and incurred-but-not-reported (IBNR) claims.

title: Policy Holder Rights
body: Legal entitlements of an insured person under an insurance policy, including the right to clear disclosure, timely claim processing, appeal of denials, and protection under consumer protection laws.

title: Subrogation
body: The legal right of an insurance company to pursue a third party that is responsible for a loss in order to recover money it paid to the insured for that loss. Allows risk transfer.
